records.name: Arch Street Friends Meeting
aka: Monthly Meeting of Friends of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Old City where people sit together in silent worship on Sunday mornings, in person or on Zoom. Families can use a children's program during the school year.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship, the monthly adult education series, or the Wednesday evening worship on Zoom. Greeters welcome newcomers on Sundays, and refreshments follow worship. Ask the office how to get involved in the meeting's committee and outreach work.

schedule.text: Sunday worship from 10:30 to 11:30 am, in person or on Zoom as a separate session, plus Wednesday worship from 5:30 to 6:30 pm on Zoom. A children's meeting runs on the first to third Sundays from September to June, 10:30 to 11:15 am.

cost.text: No cost is listed on the meeting's site.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am. Free childcare is available on site for younger children during worship.
first_step.basis: The site says newcomers are welcome, greeters meet people on Sundays, and it describes adult education and a children's program open to families.

records.notes: The home page memorial notice is dated 'Mon October 12' with no year, so it is not used as a dated sign of life. Children's meeting days differ: the site says first to third Sundays, the PYM listing says first and third. Visitor rules for Meeting for Business are not stated.

records.name: Central Philadelphia Friends Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting that worships on Sunday mornings in the meetinghouse at Friends Center in Center City, in person or on Zoom. It offers children's religious education and toddler childcare during the school year.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 11 am, or ask about youth religious education and childcare for toddlers. The site invites visitors and newcomers to worship whether or not they are members, and it lists committees on peace and social concerns, pastoral care, and community life.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am at 1501 Cherry Street or on Zoom. Youth religious education and toddler childcare are offered during the school year, except in summer.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am, or email the office for the Zoom link.
first_step.basis: The site has a page for visitors and a separate invitation for newcomers, and it says people are welcome to worship whether or not they are members.

records.notes: The PYM monthly meetings page gives 1515 Cherry Street. The meeting's own site and Friends Center both give 1501 Cherry Street, which is used here. The site names First Day School but gives no times or ages, and lists committees with no joining details. The site has no dated items, and its copyright year is not used.

records.name: West Philadelphia Friends Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker worship group in West Philadelphia that meets for silent worship on the first and third Sundays of the month, in person or on Zoom.
records.what_you_do: Join silent worship on the first and third Sundays at Calvary Center or on Zoom. The site lists no children's program, no childcare, and no committees or volunteer work open to visitors.

schedule.text: Sunday worship from 10:30 to 11:30 am on the first and third Sundays of each month, in person and on Zoom, under the meeting's 2026 to 2027 schedule.

locations.label: Calvary Center, upstairs Samaritan Room, enter from 48th Street

first_step.how: Come to worship on a first or third Sunday at 10:30 am. Enter from 48th Street and go upstairs to the Samaritan Room.
first_step.basis: Worship is open to the public with a clear time, a room, and a Zoom option, but the site does not describe a welcome for newcomers.

records.notes: Basis for active is the 2026 to 2027 worship schedule on the site. The site's only dated post is from 2023, read from its web address, so it is not used. The PYM listing says Sunday 10:30 with no First Day School and no childcare. The site's first and third Sunday schedule is used. The site lists no phone or email, so the contacts come from the PYM listing.

records.name: Germantown Monthly Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Germantown that worships on Sunday mornings, in person or on Zoom. Its 2023 report describes a children's program for elementary-age kids and a monthly Sunday food distribution it hosts.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 10:30 am at the Coulter Street meetinghouse or on Zoom. Ask about the monthly Sunday food distribution the meeting hosts for The Center for Returning Citizens, and about adult classes, which in 2023 included speakers, book readings, and films.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am at 47 West Coulter Street, in person or on Zoom. Elementary-age children have First Day School in person, and childcare is offered for the youngest children.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am, in person or on Zoom. Call or email the meeting with questions before your first visit.
first_step.basis: Worship is open with a clear time, two ways to attend, and a phone and email contact. The site could not be read, so a newcomer welcome could not be confirmed.

records.notes: The meeting's own site failed on two tries with a TLS certificate error, so the schedule and contacts come from the PYM directory. The 2023 state of the meeting report is the only detailed source for First Day School, classes and the food distribution, and it gives no First Day School times. The Philadelphia Quarterly Meeting save the date page lists a gathering at this meeting on January 24, 2027, 10:30 am to 4 pm, with no publication date shown. A search snippet says August gatherings move to Green Street Meeting, which was not confirmed.

records.name: Chestnut Hill Monthly Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Chestnut Hill with Sunday worship in its meetinghouse and on Zoom, a Sunday School, hymn singing, and adult classes. The site invites anyone to join.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 10:30 am, a hymn sing on the third, fourth, and fifth Sundays at 9:30 am, or an adult class on most first and second Sundays from September to May. Children join Sunday School at 10:45 am. Email the worship contact to get the Zoom link.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am in the meetinghouse or on Zoom. Sunday School runs from 10:45 to 11:30 am, hymn singing is at 9:30 am on the third to fifth Sundays, and adult classes meet most first and second Sundays from September to May.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am, or email the worship contact for the Zoom link.
first_step.basis: The site says the meeting welcomes everyone to join and gives a clear way in: attend Sunday worship or request the Zoom link.

records.notes: The site has no dated items. Dates that appear only in image file paths are not used. Childcare is listed on the PYM directory page. The site names no committees open to visitors.

records.name: Green Street Friends Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting on West School House Lane in Northwest Philadelphia with Sunday worship in person and online, a children's Sunday school, and a library that visitors can use. It says it welcomes all people.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 10:30 am, in person or online, then stay for conversation and food. Visitors can use the meeting library, which the site says is open to visitors, and can email the secretary for the online worship link.

schedule.text: Sunday worship from 10:30 to 11:30 am in person and online, with First Day School from 10:30 to 11:15 am. The PYM directory also lists Wednesday worship at 8:30 am.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am. Email the secretary to get the online link or to join the Sunday email list.
first_step.basis: The site says visitors are welcome to worship and gives an email contact for the Sunday list and online worship.

records.notes: Status is dormant by the dated-evidence rule: the newest dated item on the site is a July 2022 newsletter, even though worship times are posted and the PYM directory lists them. Owner should decide whether that label fits a worship group that still meets. The Wednesday 8:30 am worship time comes from the PYM directory only. No committees or volunteer roles are listed.

records.name: Byberry Monthly Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Northeast Philadelphia with Sunday worship and a Sunday school for children. Visitors can call or email the meeting before a first visit.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 11 am, or bring children to the Sunday school at 10 am. The meeting lists no committees or volunteer work open to visitors.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am, with Sunday school at 10 am. The directory does not list ages for the Sunday school.

first_step.how: Call or email the meeting before your first visit to ask about Sunday worship and the Sunday school.
first_step.basis: The PYM directory gives a Sunday worship time and a phone and email contact, which is a clear way in. The meeting's own site could not be read, so no newcomer welcome could be confirmed.

records.notes: The meeting's own site failed on two tries with a TLS certificate name mismatch, so every fact comes from the undated PYM directory page. Ask the meeting about its current worship and children's program before recommending it to a family. The PYM listing gives the email in a second spelling in its special notes; the first spelling is used.

records.name: Frankford Monthly Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Frankford with Sunday worship at its meetinghouse and by Zoom, a First Day School on Sundays, and family worship on fifth Sundays. The meeting's own page says children are welcome.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 10:30 am, in person or by Zoom (email the meeting for the link). On fifth Sundays, children stay with the adults for worship and activities built around a theme. The monthly business meeting is held on third Sundays after worship.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am at 1500 Orthodox Street, in person, with Zoom worship also offered. First Day School meets at 10:30 am on Sundays. Family worship is on fifth Sundays.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am, or email the meeting for the Zoom link.
first_step.basis: Worship is open with a clear time, place and contact, and the meeting's page says children are welcome. It does not describe a newcomer welcome.

records.notes: The PYM directory says First Day School and childcare are suspended because of the pandemic, but the meeting's own legacy page does not say so and lists First Day School at 10:30 am. Confirm before a family visit. The legacy page has no dated items. A separate mailing address is on the PYM page and is not published here. The own-site address on the PYM page did not resolve. Frankford Friends School (PreK to 8) is under the care of the meeting and is listed as a lead.

records.name: Friends Center (1501 Cherry Street)
records.summary: The Quaker building at 1501 Cherry Street that houses Philadelphia Yearly Meeting, Central Philadelphia Friends Meeting, and more than 20 tenant organizations. It is a building, so its public activity is listed under the groups that use it.
records.notes: Visiting: weekday hours are 7 am to 7 pm. Sunday hours appear three ways on the site (9 am to 1 pm, 10 am to 1 pm, 10 am to 2 pm), so call (215) 241-7100 first. Group tours must be booked in advance, with an honorarium requested; the visit page lists a tour contact at (215) 241-7190. The visitor can sit in the quiet worship room, use the front terrace, and browse literature in the lobby. Public events: the community calendar shows no events ('No feed items found'). The PYM venue page lists one event at Friends Center: the FWCC 90th Anniversary, Friday October 9, 2026, 6 to 8 pm, free. Open to the public is not stated, so it is not recorded as a program. The PYM calendar also lists an Interfaith Civic Day of Action (Oct 10, free, 2 to 5 pm) and a 'Welcome, Friends' talk (Oct 15, free, 7 to 8:30 pm). Neither shows a location, and the calendar shows no year, so neither is recorded.

notes: Coverage: the PYM monthly meetings list (https://www.pym.org/meetings/monthly-meetings/) was checked against the Philadelphia Quarter list (https://philadelphiaquarter.org/pqm/meetings/). Eight Quaker meetings in the City of Philadelphia have records: Arch Street, Central Philadelphia, West Philadelphia, Germantown, Chestnut Hill, Green Street, Byberry and Frankford. Unity Monthly Meeting is a lead only. All other PYM monthly meetings on the list meet outside the city (for example Abington, Haverford, Darby, Lansdowne, Radnor, Merion; Mill Creek meets in Newark, Delaware and is out of area). No independent Philadelphia Quaker worship group turned up in three searches. Budget: searches 3 of 3 used; fetches 40 of 60 used. Unreadable: the PYM a to z page and the FGC Philadelphia Quarter page returned 404 and were replaced with the PYM monthly meetings page and the Philadelphia Quarter list. Status summary: Green Street is dormant by the dated-evidence rule (July 2022 newsletter) although it posts worship times; Byberry is unknown because its own site could not be read; West Philadelphia is active only on its 2026 to 2027 schedule; Germantown and Frankford are probably active on undated or older evidence and are low confidence. Conflicts for the owner: Central Philadelphia address (1515 vs 1501 Cherry Street, 1501 used); Arch Street children's meeting days (first to third vs first and third Sundays); Frankford First Day School (suspended per PYM, not per its own page); Friends Center Sunday hours (three versions). Skipped as not community groups: Gender Justice Fund and Stockton Rush Bartol Foundation (grantmakers), Tract Association and Friends Publishing Corporation (publishers), Attorneys of the Philadelphia Defenders Association UAW Local 5502 (union), Community Ventures (business lending), Tri-College Consortium Philly Program (college program), Friends Council on Education and Friends Child Care Center (schools and child care), Friends World Committee for Consultation Section of the Americas (regional network), and Philadelphia Yearly Meeting itself (regional body). Personal details in the 2023 Germantown report (member deaths, a member's death in violence) were deliberately not recorded.
